system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer-side review.** The Seller’s claims that its terms are “market”, agreed or “FINAL” are not evidence of Buyer approval. The numerical counterproposals below are recommended negotiating positions, not agreed terms. This review is based on the supplied summaries, not the underlying SPA or DD documents.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | Meaningful general warranty recovery, with separate protection for fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and available security; a 20% cap should not be accepted merely because Seller calls it market. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000** individually; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, with only excess recoverable. | Lower thresholds, aggregation of related claims and a tipping basket; exclusions for protected claim categories. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 120,000 tipping basket**, aggregating related claims; the current combination leaves substantial losses with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | General warranties: **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least two annual reporting cycles to identify general warranty breaches, with separate periods for other categories. | **Seek 24 months**, reasonable notice requirements and preservation of timely notified contingent claims; reject blanket application to all Claims. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title receive the same cap and time limit as general warranties. | Separate protection for ownership, capacity, authority and unencumbered transfer of all shares. | **Seek a 100% price cap (AUD 24m), no thresholds and a materially longer period**, appropriately documented under NSW law; defective title threatens the entire acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception is identified. | Express preservation of remedies for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation and deliberate concealment, including attributable conduct by Seller representatives. | **Require an overriding carve-out from caps, thresholds, contractual time bars, disclosure/knowledge defences and remedy restrictions**, preserving non-excludable rights; fraud must not benefit from negotiated liability protections. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, Accounts, registers and public records, alongside specific disclosures. | Only matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope should qualify relevant warranties. | **Reject blanket disclosure; require specific warranty mapping and a frozen, indexed disclosure record**, with any permitted general disclosures narrowly defined; mere availability is not meaningful disclosure. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters Buyer or advisers knew, including matters discoverable from data room or public records. | No constructive/imputed knowledge exclusion; preferably no knowledge defence beyond agreed fair disclosure. | **Delete; fallback to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer personnel only**, excluding adviser imputation and duties of enquiry; discoverability otherwise transfers diligence risk wholesale to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent, despite associated conditions not being evidenced as satisfied. | Effective change-control consent, with contractual conditions satisfied and no unacceptable amendments, charges or termination exposure. | **Make satisfactory consent and satisfaction of its conditions a Buyer-waivable completion condition**, supported by evidence; approximately 30% of revenue is exposed. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Debt repaid at Completion and binding discharge/release arrangements covering all relevant security and guarantees. | **Require a lender payoff letter, direct repayment through completion funds flow and effective release mechanics**, with debt deducted once under the price adjustment; Buyer should not acquire unreleased secured debt. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | Conditional Completion bonuses of **AUD 420,000** omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller bears the economic cost of transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable employer on-costs, while employee entitlements are honoured. | **Quantify and expressly allocate these amounts through funds flow/price adjustment, backed by a specific indemnity**, without double counting; omission otherwise shifts Seller’s transaction costs to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 recorded open, with no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Evidence that all conditions to IP transfer are satisfied, a valid chain of title and protection against resulting ownership/use claims. | **Require verified payment and confirmatory assignment before Completion, plus a broader specific indemnity and appropriate retention**; paying an invoice alone may not resolve ownership or downstream loss. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, said not to be material; access, scope and notification obligations remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, containment, preservation of evidence, legal assessment and allocation of pre-Completion incident liabilities to Seller. | **Require investigation milestones, reporting covenants and a specific indemnity with suitable security**, escalating to a completion condition if findings warrant; uncertainty does not establish either immateriality or a confirmed notifiable breach. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals, **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assessment of the related commitments together, including timing, authority, cancellation rights, accruals and future benefit. | **Review DD-008/DD-011 together and prohibit further unapproved commitments; allocate costs according to their substance**, not automatically as debt; neither “ordinary course” nor the aggregate amount resolves treatment. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, payment/completion obligations and fraud. | **Insert an express claims matrix and precedence clause**, applying each restriction only to its designated category; an omnibus limitation could neutralise negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Seller as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Independent verification of issued capital, ownership history, encumbrances, options and other rights, plus effective transfer deliverables. | **Reconcile the register with corporate records, allotments/transfers, certificates and relevant searches; obtain releases and completion documents**; the register is important evidence, not a complete title investigation. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties treated as settled under the general regime. | A dedicated pre-Completion tax indemnity and tax warranties with appropriate duration; robust IP ownership, licensing and infringement protections. | **Reopen both:** seek tax protection through relevant assessment periods plus a buffer, separate caps/thresholds, and IP terms calibrated to verified risks; general limits are not a substitute for category-specific protection. |

**Priority:** resolve Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and bonus funding before committing to completion mechanics, while ensuring the overarching limitations do not cut across those protections.
=== END ADVICE ===
